exposure: umbilical cord arterial blood gas (UABG) analysis (pH, pO2, pCO2, base excess)
cohort: The study included 240 mother-infant dyads from consecutive singleton pregnancies of at least 32 weeks gestational age, who experienced intrapartum foetal distress and were delivered at Calcutta National Medical College & Hospital.
finding: Intrapartum foetal distress is frequently accompanied by mild umbilical acidaemia, with severe acidaemia being uncommon but a strong predictor of adverse early outcomes, concentrated in sentinel events like abruption and cord prolapse.
mod_finding: 86.7% of neonates were delivered by caesarean section, and routine UABG in high-risk deliveries may curb unnecessary caesarean sections when CTG is the sole trigger.
